source.quote: On August 26th, 2025, we notified developers using the Assistants API of its deprecation and removal from the API one year later, on August 26, 2026.

tasks.reasoning:
The whole document-chat feature, in both the Python and the TS backends plus a raw HTTP call, is built on /v1/assistants and /v1/threads. That API was removed on Aug 26, 2026, so these calls fail now.

Migrate to the Responses API, with file_search over a vector store for the uploaded documents and the Conversations API (or previous_response_id) for thread state.

Some calls (assistants.files.create, file_ids) are v1 Assistants shapes that were already obsolete.

The pinned SDKs (Python 1.79.0, Node 4.100.0) may lack the Conversations resource. The migration agent should check whether a minimal SDK bump is needed, or use previous_response_id instead.

Use a current replacement model rather than gpt-4o, which is itself being retired.

record.prBody:
## Assistants API removed Aug 26, 2026; migrate to Responses and Conversations APIs [Verified]

### Change

Replaced the Assistants API (assistants, threads, runs, assistants.files and the raw HTTP /v1/assistants/{id}/files call) with vector stores, file_search and Responses in server/openai.ts, main.py and document_chat_api.py. The "assistant" is now a vector store ID, and the response ID is chained with previous_response_id. Model is now gpt-6-luna. No SDK bump: node 4.100 and python 1.79 already have responses and vector stores. Added test/responses.test.mts.

Files touched:
- `__pycache__/document_chat_api.cpython-311.pyc`
- `__pycache__/main.cpython-311.pyc`
- `document_chat_api.py`
- `main.py`
- `server/openai.ts`
- `test/responses.test.mts`

### Why

The Assistants API (/v1/assistants, /v1/threads) was removed on 2026-08-26, so every document-chat call in the Python and TS backends fails.

> On August 26th, 2025, we notified developers using the Assistants API of its deprecation and removal from the API one year later, on August 26, 2026.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | fail (17) | fail (16) | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| responses-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- responses-test, added by the agent: `npx --no-install tsx test/responses.test.mts` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_model_lookup`: pass
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_check_request: pass (responses body (model, instructions, input, previous_response_id, tools) has no unknown or deprecated params. gpt-6-luna is active.)
- openai_model_lookup: pass (gpt-6-luna is active and supports v1/responses.)

Test of this change: `responses-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The Python code was only compiled (py_compile). The openai package isn't installed in the sandbox, so the Python paths were never executed.
- client.vector_stores on openai-python 1.79.0 was not checked against the installed package.
- The Conversations API was not used. Context is chained with previous_response_id instead.
- gpt-4o is still used by the chat.completions calls in server/routes.ts, server/document-routes.ts and test-openai.js. They are out of scope, but gpt-4o retires on 2027-01-14.
- The 17 pre-existing typecheck errors were left alone.
- typecheck was already failing before the change and still fails.

### Behaviour changes

- Model changed from gpt-4o to gpt-6-luna for document chat.
- No server-side assistant or thread objects exist any more. assistantId now holds a vector store ID (vs_...). threadId is a local ID.
- Thread state lives in process memory: the last response ID and the transcript, so it is lost on restart. In the Python apps it is keyed per client_id. OpenAI stores the responses.
- Python document_chat_api.py: threadId is the local string thread_<clientId>, and /chat returns the transcript from memory, oldest first as the TS backend does. The old code reversed it, so this order differs from before.
- The Python polling loops are gone because responses.create is synchronous. The retired 'retrieval' tool and file_ids are replaced by file_search over a vector store.
- In server/openai.ts, if the vector store creation fails or the ID is simulated (not starting with vs_), the demo fallback is kept. The request then goes out without file_search.
- Mock file IDs (mock_file_...) are filtered out before the vector store is created.

---

preparation.reasoning: No codegen or prebuild steps are needed. Typecheck (tsc --noEmit) and build (vite build, then esbuild) work directly from the installed dependencies. Nothing in package.json (no postinstall, prepare, or generate script) needs to run. review.summary: Every Assistants call site is replaced: assistants become vector stores, and threads become locally held `previous_response_id` chains for `responses.create` with `file_search`. That covers all named beta.* call sites and the raw POST /v1/assistants fetch. The chat.completions sites are not affected by this removal and are rightly left alone. The `verified` grade overstates the evidence, though. Typecheck still fails (16 errors). The new test only greps the Python files and mocks the TS SDK, so no Python path runs and no live call is made. The diff also swaps the model to `gpt-6-luna` everywhere, changes chat-history ordering in `document_chat_api.py`, moves conversation state into process memory, and commits `.pyc` files.

concerns.issue: MODEL changes from `gpt-4o` to `gpt-6-luna` in all three files. The Assistants removal does not require this, and the old TS comment explicitly said not to change the model unless requested. I could not confirm `gpt-6-luna` is a valid model ID. The test asserts this string against a mock, so it proves nothing about the live API. Check the OpenAI models list, or keep `gpt-4o`.

Message order flips. `messages.list` returned newest first and the old code reversed it, so clients got oldest first. The new local transcript is oldest first, and the unchanged `[::-1]` now returns newest first. `server/openai.ts` dropped its `.reverse()` and keeps oldest-first order, so the two backends now disagree.

Conversation context used to live server-side in OpenAI threads. It is now an in-memory Map/dict that grows without bound, is lost on restart, and is not shared across workers. `sendMessage` silently starts a fresh context for an unknown threadId. Concurrent messages on the same thread race on `lastResponseId`. The change notice points to the Conversations API, which would keep context persistent; it was not used.

Vector store ingestion of `file_ids` is asynchronous. A chat sent right after upload may run `file_search` before indexing finishes and return ungrounded answers. Consider `createAndPoll` or checking `file_counts` before returning.

`vectorStores` and `responses` (`vector_stores` and `responses` in Python) exist only in newer SDK versions. The old code used `beta.assistants.files`, which suggests an older pinned SDK. The diff does not bump either dependency. Typecheck still has 16 errors, and it is unclear whether any are in `server/openai.ts`. The build passing does not imply a typecheck pass.

The Python files are only regex-checked for `responses.create` and the absence of `beta.*`. Neither Flask route is executed, so bugs there (e.g. the reused `thread_id` variable now holding a dict) are untested. The TS path is fully mocked, and no test covers the vector-store fallback (`asst_` id, no tools) or an `incomplete` status.
Compiled bytecode files are committed. Remove them and add `__pycache__/` to `.gitignore`.

If every file ID is a `mock_file_` placeholder, it creates an empty vector store. `sendMessage` then still attaches `file_search` because the id starts with `vs_`. This is harmless but wasteful, and those stores are never deleted.

checkFirst: Confirm `gpt-6-luna` is a real, available model, or revert to `gpt-4o`.

change.title: GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini snapshots shut down Jan 14, 2027; migrate to gpt-6-luna

source.quote: On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses the "gpt-4o" alias everywhere. The "which was released May 13 ... do not change this unless explicitly requested" comment is boilerplate. The alias points at the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 / 2024-11-20 snapshots, which are removed Jan 14, 2027, so the alias is expected to stop working. Replace it with gpt-6-luna, or another current model, in all chat.completions calls and remove the stale comment.

Uncertain: whether OpenAI keeps the bare alias alive. The migration agent should assume it does not.

The assistant model sites are also covered by the Assistants migration task. Avoid conflicting edits there and just make sure the replacement model is not gpt-4o.

callSites.why: chat.completions.create with model "gpt-4o". The alias resolves to a gpt-4o-2024-08-06/11-20 snapshot that is being removed.
Pinned model "gpt-4o" for the assistant. This is being rewritten by the Assistants migration, which should pick the replacement model.
Assistant created with model "gpt-4o". Coordinate with the Assistants migration.

Replaced "gpt-4o" with "gpt-6-luna" in server/document-routes.ts, server/routes.ts, server/openai.ts, test-openai.js, main.py and document_chat_api.py. Removed the stale "do not change" comments. Switched max_tokens to max_completion_tokens on the chat.completions calls. Added test-model.mjs, registered as the check model-proof. dist/ build output is untouched.

- `server/document-routes.ts`
- `server/openai.ts`
- `server/routes.ts`
- `test-model.mjs`
- `test-openai.js`

### Why

The gpt-4o alias resolves to snapshots that shut down on 2027-01-14. The replacement, gpt-6-luna, is a reasoning model and rejects max_tokens.

> On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |

- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_check_request: pass (chat.completions with gpt-6-luna and max_completion_tokens: model active, no deprecated or unknown params)

Test of this change: `model-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The Assistants calls (beta.assistants and beta.threads in main.py, document_chat_api.py and server/openai.ts) only had the model string swapped. The Assistants API is removed 2026-08-26 and needs its own migration to Responses.
- Whether gpt-6-luna works with the Assistants API was not checked.
- The typecheck already failed before this change (pre-existing errors); I did not re-run it or the build after the edit.
- dist/ is stale build output and will be regenerated by the build.
- typecheck was already failing before the change and still fails.

### Behaviour changes

- Model is now gpt-6-luna. Output quality, latency and cost may differ.
- gpt-6-luna is a reasoning model, so its output-token cap now covers reasoning tokens as well as visible output. The small max_completion_tokens: 10 in test-openai.js may return empty content.

---

## openai (npm) 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22 [Needs review]

### Change

Upgraded openai 4.100.0 -> ^7.49.0 via npm. Fixed the two beta.threads.runs.retrieve calls in server/openai.ts to the named-param form (runId, {thread_id}). Added engines.node ">=22" in package.json and bumped .replit nodejs-18 to nodejs-22. Added test/openai-v7.test.mjs (checks the installed version, the Node version and engines, and that a stubbed-fetch runs.retrieve hits /threads/t1/runs/run_1).

Files touched:
- `.replit`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `server/openai.ts`
- `test/openai-v7.test.mjs`

### Why

openai 7.x requires Node.js 22, and crossing majors 5-7 changed the signature of runs.retrieve (thread_id moved into params).

> * require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | fail (17) | fail (17) | 8 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| openai-v7 | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 8

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- openai-v7, added by the agent: `node test/openai-v7.test.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `openai-v7`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Deploy host Node version must be 22+ (only .replit was updated; no Dockerfile or CI found)
- Assistants API is removed 2026-08-26, so assistants paths in server/openai.ts need their own migration to Responses; assistants.files.create still fails to typecheck (pre-existing)

change.title: openai (PyPI) 3.0.0 switches default HTTP client to HTTPX2; httpx no longer installed

source.quote: HTTPX2 is now the default HTTP client, and `httpx` is no longer installed automatically.

tasks.reasoning:
The Python app pins openai 1.79.0 (uv.lock), below both the 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 majors. Nothing breaks today, but the SDK is two majors behind, and the Assistants migration may need a newer SDK.

In 3.0.0, HTTPX2 becomes the default HTTP client and httpx is no longer installed automatically. Anything in the repo that imports httpx directly, or passes http_client=httpx.Client, needs httpx added explicitly or adapting.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- openai:pypi-2-0-0 (sdk-major): openai (PyPI) 2.0.0: function call output types may now be arrays, not only strings, effective 2025-09-30. Moving from 1.79.0 to 3.x crosses the 2.0.0 major. Its change (function call outputs may be arrays) is handled within the same bump. The repo currently reads no function-call output, but the migration agent should check any new Responses code written for the Assistants migration.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-python/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "This may break existing callsites that assume `output` is always a string."

record.prBody:
## openai (PyPI) 3.0.0 switches default HTTP client to HTTPX2; httpx no longer installed [Not affected]

### Change

No code changes. The Python code (main.py, document_chat_api.py) uses only the module-level openai client. A search found no httpx import and no http_client= argument anywhere in the repo's Python files.

No files changed.

### Why

The 3.0.0 change swaps the default HTTP client from httpx to HTTPX2, so only code that imports httpx or passes a custom http_client breaks. This repo does neither. pyproject.toml pins openai>=1.79.0 and uv.lock has 1.79.0, so nothing changes until the SDK is bumped. The 2.0.0 array-output change doesn't apply because the repo reads no function-call output.

> HTTPX2 is now the default HTTP client, and `httpx` is no longer installed automatically.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-python/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | fail (17) | fail (17) | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- I did not bump the SDK to 3.x or run the Python code on it.
- The Assistants API calls in these files (beta.assistants.files.create, threads, runs) are removed on 2026-08-26 and need a separate Responses API migration. I left them alone, along with the gpt-4o model, which retires on 2027-01-14.
- typecheck was already failing before the change and still fails.

### Behaviour changes

None intended.
